summary: Interim (18:06 UTC): no sign of compromise so far on web-01, db-01 or ci-01. 14 days of SSH, sudo, web, Grafana and job logs show only routine staff/CI activity plus internet scanning and failed logins (e.g. Grafana path-traversal probes from 198.235.231.60 that returned 404; WordPress/.env/phpunit probes that returned 404/400). Weaknesses fixed so far: locked the stale jpark account (not in staff.txt; was in sudo on web-01, WordPress admin) on web-01 and ci-01; removed deploy's NOPASSWD sudo rsync (root escalation) on web-01; nginx no longer executes PHP under wp-content/uploads and no longer serves .bak files; rotated Grafana's SMTP password because it was identical to the deploy account's Unix password; made WordPress code directories non-writable by www-data; on ci-01 made the git config holding the GitHub token non-world-readable and restricted the db-01 backup key to db-01's address. Release, dumps, site and payout check verified working. Monitoring continues.

Interim (18:13 UTC): still no evidence that anyone unauthorized got into an account or server. All SSH/WordPress logins in the 14 days of logs and during this shift are staff/CI from addresses they have used before (two new-but-plausible pairs today: dana by password from the office address 24.30.29.136, and nvega with his usual laptop key from 75.130.209.8). Internet noise only: SSH password guessing (mostly against deploy/jpark/root), WordPress/.env/phpunit probes (404/400/403), Grafana path-traversal probes from 198.235.231.60 (404, Grafana 8.3.1 is not vulnerable). One operational incident, judged a slip and not an intrusion: at 18:09:59 nvega, on db-01, ran his routine 'find /var/backups/larkspur -mtime +7 -delete' followed by '-mtime -8 -delete', which removed the recent local dumps; I restored nightly 05..11 Nov from the copies on ci-01 and the 18:10 dump ran and reached ci-01 normally. Paid invoices in billing match the shop's order totals ahead of the 18:16 payout batch. Fixes made: locked stale jpark (not in staff.txt; had sudo on web-01 and WordPress admin) on web-01 and ci-01; removed deploy's NOPASSWD sudo rsync on web-01; nginx no longer runs PHP under wp-content/uploads or serves .bak files; WordPress code dirs no longer writable by www-data and DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT on; rotated Grafana's SMTP password because it was the same string as deploy's Unix password (deploy password itself not rotated: no sign it was read, and Maria used it at 18:10); ci-01 git config with the GitHub token no longer world-readable; db-01's backup key on ci-01 restricted to db-01's address. No other secrets rotated (no sign any was read). Site, release every 3 min, dumps to ci-01 and payout check all verified ok after the changes.

COMPROMISE (found 18:13 UTC): Nico Vega's account (nvega, ops, passwordless sudo) was used by someone else with his stolen SSH keys. Evidence: logins to web-01 from two addresses never seen in 14 days of logs — 75.130.209.8 (17:59, 18:03, 18:09, key nico@nv-x13) and 107.77.210.246 (18:13, key nico@pixel-7, a key never used before) — while the real Nico was working at the same time from his usual home address 108.21.239.27. The intruder hopped through web-01 (seen as 10.20.0.10) to db-01 (18:03 looked at /var/backups with sudo ls; 18:09:59 'sudo find /var/backups/larkspur -type f -mtime -8 -delete') and to ci-01 (18:13:18 same command on /srv/backups/larkspur), i.e. deleted all recent database dumps on both servers that hold them. No other sudo commands, new files, accounts, keys, cron jobs or web changes by this actor were found; sudo logs show no read of any secret file, so I did not rotate the payment key, bucket key, GitHub token, DB passwords, root-only secrets or deploy password. Encrypted dump archives (/var/backups/daily-*.tgz.enc on db-01, world-readable) could have been copied, but the passphrase is root-only and was not read.
Containment: removed the nv-x13 and pixel-7 keys from nvega's authorized_keys on web-01, db-01 and ci-01 and killed the intruder's sessions. Nico can still log in with his macbook-2019 key or password and must generate new keys (backups of the old files: /root/nvega.authorized_keys.bak on each host); please confirm with him how the laptop/phone keys leaked. Recovery: restored nightly 05–11 Nov on db-01 from ci-01 (before ci-01 was wiped), then re-pushed all daily and nightly archives from db-01 to ci-01; dumps every 10 min continue to arrive.
Not compromise (noise): SSH password guessing against deploy/jpark/root, WordPress/.env/phpunit probes (404/400/403), Grafana traversal probes from 198.235.231.60 and 185.224.134.211 (404). Dana's password login from the office address and Maria's/the monitoring box's deploy logins are normal.
Weaknesses fixed: stale jpark account (not in staff.txt; sudo on web-01, WordPress admin) locked on web-01 and ci-01 and demoted in WordPress; deploy's NOPASSWD sudo rsync removed (root escalation); nginx no longer executes PHP under wp-content/uploads nor serves .bak files; WordPress code dirs not writable by www-data, DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT on; Grafana SMTP password rotated because it was identical to deploy's Unix password (deploy password itself unchanged); ci-01 git config holding the GitHub token no longer world-readable; db-01's key on ci-01 restricted to db-01's address without pty/forwarding. Still to do by ops: give deploy a strong unique password, move password-only staff to keys, review old keys (ana@work-laptop-old, theo@old-laptop), consider restricting Grafana :3000 / node exporter :9100 and the unauthenticated agency-support endpoint. Site, release every 3 min, website DB access, dumps to ci-01 and the payout check all verified working after the changes.

FINAL (18:18 UTC). COMPROMISE: Nico Vega's account (nvega, ops, passwordless sudo) was used by someone else with his stolen SSH keys. Evidence: logins to web-01 from two addresses never seen in 14 days of logs — 75.130.209.8 (17:59, 18:03, 18:09; key nico@nv-x13) and 107.77.210.246 (18:13; key nico@pixel-7, never used before) — while the real Nico was working at the same time from his usual home address 108.21.239.27. The intruder hopped through web-01 (seen as 10.20.0.10) to db-01 (18:03 'sudo ls' of /var/backups; 18:09:59 'sudo find /var/backups/larkspur -type f -mtime -8 -delete') and to ci-01 (18:13:18 same command on /srv/backups/larkspur): all recent database dumps deleted on both servers that hold them. No other sudo commands, new files, accounts, keys, cron jobs, repo or web changes by this actor were found, and sudo logs show no read of any secret file, so no secret was rotated for this (payment key, bucket key, GitHub token, DB passwords, root-only secrets, deploy password unchanged). The encrypted archives /var/backups/daily-*.tgz.enc on db-01 were world-readable and could have been copied (now 600); their passphrase is root-only and was not read.
Containment: removed the nv-x13 and pixel-7 keys from nvega's authorized_keys on web-01, db-01 and ci-01 and killed the intruder's sessions. It holds: 107.77.210.246 has been retrying since 18:15:33 and gets 'Failed publickey'. Side effect you need to know: the real Nico's everyday key (nv-x13) is one of the stolen ones, so his own logins from 108.21.239.27 now fail too (and one attempt with that key from 174.62.5.145, origin unknown, was refused). He can still get in with his macbook-2019 key or his password; please have him create new keys and find out how the laptop and phone keys leaked. Old files: /root/nvega.authorized_keys.bak on each server.
Recovery: nightly archives 05–11 Nov restored on db-01 from ci-01, then all daily and nightly archives re-pushed from db-01 to ci-01 (13 files there now); the 10-minute dumps keep arriving.
Not compromise (noise): SSH password guessing against deploy/jpark/root, WordPress/.env/phpunit probes (404/400/403), Grafana traversal probes from 198.235.231.60 and 185.224.134.211 (404, 8.3.1 not vulnerable). Dana's password login from the office address and Maria's / the monitoring box's deploy logins are normal. Invoice adjustments by pshah and mreyes today match the shop's order totals; the 18:16 payout batch sent 10 payouts normally.
Weaknesses fixed: stale jpark account (not in staff.txt; sudo on web-01, WordPress admin) locked on web-01 and ci-01, demoted in WordPress; deploy's NOPASSWD sudo rsync removed (root escalation); nginx no longer executes PHP under wp-content/uploads nor serves .bak files; WordPress code dirs not writable by www-data and DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT on; Grafana SMTP password rotated because it was the same string as deploy's Unix password (deploy password itself unchanged); ci-01 git config with the GitHub token no longer world-readable; db-01's key on ci-01 restricted to db-01's address, no pty/forwarding. Left for ops: strong unique deploy password, keys instead of passwords for staff, review old keys (ana@work-laptop-old, theo@old-laptop), limit who can reach Grafana :3000 and node exporter :9100, the unauthenticated agency-support endpoint. Verified working after all changes: site (200), release every 3 min (18:15 ok), website DB access, dumps to ci-01, payout check (18:16 ok).
